extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants, peer reviewers, Scientific Review Administrators (SRAs), and NIH extramural staff
extracted.subtask_short: NIH peer review of grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and policy statements governing how NIH grant and training applications are reviewed, scored, and escalated through initial Scientific Review Groups and second-level advisory councils, including special review topics (human subjects, inclusion, safety, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective of initial peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of the initial peer review is to evaluate and rate the scientific and technical merit of the proposed research or research training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial review evaluates scientific/technical merit and results in ratings used to inform funding decisions; managed by the Office of Extramural Research (OER).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial review by Scientific Review Groups (SRGs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review of applications submitted to the NIH takes place in multiple steps. The initial step of the peer review process takes place in Scientific Review Groups (SRGs) that are managed by Scientific Review Administrators (SRAs) who are located in the Institutes and Centers that are components of the NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRGs (also called study sections) conduct the first-pass scientific/technical evaluation for investigator-initiated and solicited applications; SRAs manage these groups within NIH components.

rubrics_metrics.name: IC Review Branches for special solicitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Review Branches of the awarding institutes and centers (ICs) manage scientific review groups that evaluate applications submitted in response to special solicitations such as Request for Applications (RFAs), and for unique programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications responding to RFAs or unique program solicitations may be reviewed by IC-managed review groups rather than CSR-managed SRGs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-level review by NIH National Advisory Councils
rubrics_metrics.description: The second level of peer review is carried out by the NIH National Advisory Councils.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These Councils provide a second-layer of review to advise on funding recommendations and policy considerations following SRG evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory councils composition and public representation
rubrics_metrics.description: These Councils are composed of scientists from the extramural research community and public representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Councils ensure that the NIH receives advice from a cross-section of the US population in the process of its deliberation and decisions; rosters and meeting schedules are maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rating of grant applications / explicit review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH Announces New Explicit Statements of Review Criteria (Rating of Grant Applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH has issued explicit statements of review criteria (see Announcement, June 1997) guiding reviewers on dimensions to consider when rating applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: CSR Scoring Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: CSR Scoring Procedure is identified as a distinct component of the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural guidance on how CSR implements scores for applications (refer to CSR Scoring Procedure document linked on the page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for Reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: General 'Guidelines for Reviewers' are provided to direct reviewer conduct and evaluation practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains expectations for reviewer behavior, evaluation standards, and procedural rules for SRG meetings (see linked Guidelines for Reviewers document).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Procedures for Scientific Review Group Meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures that govern how SRG meetings are conducted and how reviews are performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes operational rules for study section meetings, conflict of interest handling, discussion and scoring processes (see linked Review Procedures document).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for Review of Specific Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialized guidance for reviewing particular application types (e.g., new investigator R01s, modular grants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate guidance documents address the unique considerations and review criteria applicable to specific application categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of New Investigator R01s
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific review guidance and procedures tailored to R01 applications from new investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses special considerations to fairly evaluate early-career investigators (see 'Review of New Investigator R01's' link).

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlined Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Streamlined Review is identified as a review approach/procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural option intended to make review more efficient under certain conditions; see linked 'Streamlined Review' guidance for applicability and process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular Grant Application and Award
rubrics_metrics.description: Modular Grant Application and Award is a specific application/award format referenced in peer review guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impacts budget presentation and possibly review considerations for modular-budget applications (see linked document).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of human subjects and human-subjects evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions to Reviewers for Evaluating Research Involving Human Subjects in Grant and Cooperative Agreement Applications (April 5, 2002) and related decision trees and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must evaluate protections for human subjects, inclusion criteria, consent, and related ethical safeguards; specific instruction documents and decision trees are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion policies (children, women, minorities) in clinical research
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple documents addressing inclusion: 'Inclusion of Children as Participants in Research Involving Human Subjects', 'Women in Clinical Research', 'Minorities in Clinical Research', and NIH-Defined Phase III clinical trials inclusion guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must consider whether applications appropriately address inclusion of children, women, and minorities (and adherence to NIH policies), with supporting PowerPoint and PDF resources linked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Safety Monitoring Plans in Clinical Trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on reviewing Data and Safety Monitoring Plans for clinical trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess whether appropriate monitoring plans are proposed to ensure participant safety and data integrity; resources provided in PDF/PowerPoint formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of research involving natural products (complex mixtures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for review of research involving natural products usually prepared as complex mixtures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers special review considerations where standard product characterization may be limited; see linked document for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review Oversight Group (PROG) oversight functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The function of the Peer Review Oversight Group (PROG) is to advise and make recommendations on the development and implementation of policies pertaining to the monitoring of, coordination of, and evaluation of peer review conducted at the NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PROG ensures review processes keep pace with advances in research and that peer reviewer expertise is appropriate for scientific needs; PROG meeting minutes and roster are maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workgroups to address regulatory burdens
rubrics_metrics.description: Workgroups established to address regulatory burdens associated with peer review and extramural policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates NIH convenes targeted workgroups to identify and mitigate regulatory/process burdens affecting peer review and applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of public representatives/participants in scientific peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit attention to including public representatives/participants in scientific peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH policy encourages or provides for public representation in review processes to increase transparency and public perspective (see 'Inclusion of Public Representatives/Participants in Scientific Peer Review').
